newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 7.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- Toys R Us said comparable store sales for the holiday season were flat.
- Monsanto agreed to buy Holden's Foundation Seeds and its sales agents for up to $1.02 billion.
- Raytheon's proposed purchase of Texas Instruments' defense operations for $2.95 billion suggests the firm sees its long term future in defense.
- Ford reported an 11 percent rise in December sales.
- Nissan will offer buyout packages to 2,500 North American employees.
- Laidlaw agreed to buy American Medical Response for $1.12 billion.
- A Vanguard fund that tracks the S&P 500 has been moving up the ranks of the largest stock funds, and could eventually challenge Magellan's No. 1 ranking.
- Apple said it won't immediately drop its current operating system as it moves to a new one based on its Next acquisition.
- The Los Angeles Dodgers said the franchise is up for sale.
- Agouron will distribute the first protease inhibitor designed for HIV infected children through a government-approved giveaway program.
- Venture capitalists took a record 260 companies public in 1996 despite last summer's stock sell off.
- Prudential Insurance was fined $1 million after some Prudential offices destroyed documents related to deceptive sales suits against the firm.
- Energy futures soared on forcasts for colder weather and Iraq's planned slowing of crude oil sales.
- Heinz said it hired away the head of Campbell's U.S. soup unit, but Campbell vowed to fight the move.
- Treasury bonds fell, continuing a five-week trend.
